page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture, it provides 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance features 128 GB of DDR4 memory, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio typical of general-purpose compute profiles. Local storage is not included, requiring external cloud disk volumes, while baseline network bandwidth reaches 6 Gbps. No dedicated GPU hardware accelerators are present on this instance type.

In synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates average multi-core throughput alongside weaker single-thread execution. Multi-core performance metrics, such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, reflect solid parallel execution across its 32 vCPUs. Conversely, single-core benchmarks like Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression fall into lower percentiles due to the lower base clock speeds of its processor generation. Memory bandwidth remains steady in the average tier, supporting uncached read speeds of 98.48 GB/sec and uncached write speeds of 49.01 GB/sec.

From a resource density and cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.sn2ne.8xlarge offers a balanced resource allocation for multi-threaded enterprise applications that do not depend on high single-thread clock rates. Its high core count and 128 GB memory capacity make it suitable for parallel web serving, Redis caching nodes, software compilation pipelines, and containerized microservices. However, latency-sensitive tasks or applications heavily bound by single-core efficiency may experience performance bottlenecks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server built on x86_64 architecture, powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor at 2.5 GHz. It features 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with hyperthreading, paired with 128 GB of system memory for a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The instance includes no local storage or GPUs, relying on network-attached storage and offering a 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations highlight average multi-core processing capabilities and memory throughput, contrasted with weaker single-threaded execution due to its legacy CPU generation. This profile provides predictable multi-threaded scaling for workloads such as Redis caching clusters, static web serving, software build tasks, and general microservices hosting.
